methodology: Five-verse bounded initial screening only. Current main and prior PR #254 checked; no external primary-text collation, so no verified or publishable associations. Provisional no-specific-parallel is not evidence of absence.

records.topic: Arrogant leaders explicitly reject Ṣāliḥ's message
records.notes: The quoted response belongs to the Qur'anic Ṣāliḥ narrative. Generic opposition to prophets is insufficient as a source-specific antecedent.

records.topic: The she-camel is hamstrung and challengers demand threatened punishment
records.notes: The miraculous she-camel episode requires independently dated pre-Islamic textual attestation. Do not treat ancient Thamūd ethnonyms or camel depictions as evidence of this narrative.

records.topic: A destructive shaking seizes the people, leaving them fallen in their dwellings
records.notes: Earthquake or disaster motifs are widespread; no precisely matched independently dated destruction account has been established in this pass.

records.topic: Ṣāliḥ turns away, saying he conveyed his Lord's message and counseled them
records.notes: No earlier source-specific witness to this speech established; generic rejected-prophet farewells do not qualify.

records.topic: Lot condemns an unprecedented indecency among his people
records.notes: Genesis 19:1–11 is an important earlier Lot narrative comparison to inspect, but it depicts attempted assault on visitors, whereas this verse frames Lot's rebuke as a broad accusation. No original-language or critical-edition comparison performed in this batch; do not publish.

pending_questions: Compare Genesis 19:1–11 against 7:80 in identified Hebrew edition and Qur'anic Arabic, preserving differences in narrative focus.
Seek dated epigraphic references to Thamūd separately from the she-camel and catastrophe story; do not equate ethnonym with proof of the episode.
